plan.title: AD lesional vs control: DE genes and Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12000-gene Salmon-derived raw counts across 12 skin samples (6 AD-lesional, 6 control), unpaired, single batch. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which the knowledge service flags as a QC judgment call rather than an automatic exclusion: DESeq2 size factors account for depth differences, so the sample is kept through structure QC, inspected on PCA/distance/library-size plots, and only removed if it shows an independent problem (outlier clustering, identity doubt). The pipeline follows the grounded procedure: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size) -> DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the GLM -> Wald test with an explicit reference level (control) -> apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2FC -> BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering -> preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary, since both are staged locally) to answer which hallmark pathways change. A p-value histogram and MA/dispersion diagnostics accompany the DE step per the sourced reporting rules. Robustness is checked by also running edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and reporting the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence gene set, per the R-0001/R-0042 consensus for 6-per-group designs. Enrichment falls back to the ranked method only (no ORA) unless the significant gene count clears the ~50-gene threshold that gives ORA any power.

steps.method: vst(blind), PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size barplot
keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
